newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia shale oil twins say market informed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia shale oil twins say market informed.

text.p: Shale oil hopefuls Central Pacific Minerals NL and Southern Pacific Petroleum NL said on Thursday they knew of no explanation for recent rises in their share prices.
Replying to an Australian Stock Exchange price query, the companies, known as the Rundle twins, said there were no matters of importance about to be announced to shareholders or the market.
The main assets of the companies are their stakes in the Stuart shale oil deposit in central Queensland.
In September, the companies entered into an agreement with Canada's Suncor Inc to form the Stuart Energy Joint Venture to develop the deposit.
Suncor will hold 50 percent of the joint venture company while the Rundle twins will hold 25 percent each.
Under the agreement, Suncor also acquires a 22 percent stake in each of Southern Pacific Petroleum and Central Pacific Minerals.

By 12.20 p.m. (0120 GMT), Southern Pacific Petroleum shares were steady at A$2.55 on turnover of 62,495 shares, while Central Pacific Minerals was 10 cents higher at A$6.65 on turnover of 34,700 shares.
